newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: WOMAN TO MAKE CZECH CABINET "GENTLER" - PM.
newsitem.headline: WOMAN TO MAKE CZECH CABINET "GENTLER" - PM.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Monday that the first woman in his cabinet might soften the working environment, but insisted that his all-male governments since 1992 had not been unruly boys' clubs.

The three-party conservative coalition led by Klaus agreed on Monday to name Vlasta Parkanova as justice minister, replacing Jan Kalvoda who resigned last month after he admitted to using an unattained "Doctor of Law" title.
When asked at a joint briefing with the minister-designate if a woman would change how the government functions, Klaus said he supposed it might "make it more gentle".
But he added that the meetings were never rude.
Cabinet debates "have always been very gentle and decent," he said.
"I hope nobody thinks that there were things happening which a woman's ear should not hear."
Parkanova, a certified doctor of law aged 45 and currently serving as chief of staff at the interior ministry, was nominated by the junior coalition partner, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA).
She is expected to be officially confirmed by President Vaclav Havel in the coming days.
Klaus has rejected any criticism of his cabinets' lack of a woman, once telling a group of foreign jouranlists that there was not a qualified woman willing to serve in the cabinet.

Kalvoda, a parliamentary deputy and a cabinet member since the coalition was formed in 1992, was the fifth member of parliament who admitted using the title of Juris Doctor without actually having qualified for it.
Out of the other four fake doctors, only one has resigned her parliamentary seat.
